findings.title: PCA centre sample pins about 3 GiB of GPU memory for the whole mapping run
findings.where: scripts/run_mapping.py:162-174 (raw.append at 168, never deleted); same code at 60d7796:167
findings.problem: `raw.append(z.reshape(-1, clip.d)[::step])` stores a strided VIEW. Each view keeps the full per-frame buffer alive: 240x320x512 fp32 = 150 MiB. That is 20 x 150 = 3000 MiB for 200 MiB of samples. The list stays alive (on the GPU) through token extraction and the whole mapping pass. It is dead data after the centre is computed at lines 170-172.
findings.failure_scenario: The office_0 mapping peak of 4807 MiB is about 3000 MiB dead PCA buffers plus about 1.8 GiB of real work. If 'Peak GPU memory is \ph GB' (main.tex:951) is filled from peak_alloc_mib, the paper overstates memory by about 2.9 GiB. The README's root causes are wrong as a result. 'LSeg needs > 3.3 GB at the first PCA frame': LSeg weights are 1554 MiB and its activations are <= 334 MiB (4914 - 26 splats - 1554 - 3000). So the 14:20 probe must have failed near the 9th-10th PCA frame, not the first. 'Mapping memory grows with N' also misses a fixed ~3 GiB. The caps MAP_NEED=9000 (+2048 headroom = 11 GB free needed) are sized around the leak, so the test stage waits for large USGLoc gaps for no reason.
findings.evidence: 1) CPU run of the real code path (scratchpad/raw_probe.py: the current run_mapping.py with a fake extractor, downscale 2, pca-frames 20, stopped after the centre) printed: `RAW: 20 frames, 200 MiB of samples keep 3000 MiB alive`. 2) Plain check: upsample_tokens((60,80,512) -> (240,320)) then reshape(-1,512)[::15]: `storage kept alive 150.0 MiB` for `raw bytes needed 10.0 MiB`. 3) The logs fit a fixed ~3 GiB. The mapping peak is 4806 MiB with 3 keyframes (logs/smoke_mapping_3kf.log) and 4807 MiB with 179 (map_office_0.log). room_2 (954,119 G) is 5732 vs office_0 (620,290 G) 4807, so +925 MiB per 334k Gaussians = 2.9 KB/Gaussian. That leaves an N-independent part of 4807 - 620290*2.9KB = ~3.09 GiB. 4) LSeg weights measured on CPU: `LSeg net MiB 1311.8 | CLIP text MiB 242.0 | total 1553.7`.
findings.fix: After the centre loop (after line 174), add `del raw, z`. This changes no saved value, so the val fields stay valid. To also cut the PCA-phase peak, store `z.reshape(-1, clip.d)[::step].clone()` (or .cpu()). The values are the same, and zbar only enters the saved state because centre=False for Table I. Then re-measure the mapping and extraction peaks, and correct the README memory findings and the MAP_NEED cap.

findings.title: GPU reservation makes peak_alloc_extract_mib and peak_reserved_mib report the reservation, not the job
findings.where: usplat/gpu_reserve.py:31-33; scripts/run_mapping.py:232-233, 281-282, 312-317; scripts/eval_seg.py:519-523 with usplat/runlog.py memory peaks
findings.problem: apply() allocates one tensor of cap-512 MiB and frees it. torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() counts that allocation, and nothing resets the peak before run_mapping.py:232 reads it. The reset at line 282 sets the reserved peak to the current reserved memory, which includes the cached block. Both fields therefore hold the reservation size from commit cc65f08 on.
findings.failure_scenario: MAP_NEED=9000 gives frac = 9000/16303 (nvidia-smi total), and the cap = frac x 15.46 GiB (torch total) = 8739 MiB. The reservation is 8739-512 = 8227 MiB. So every test-scene map log will show peak_alloc_extract_mib >= 8227 and peak_reserved_mib >= 8227, where the val logs (made at 5b21781, no reservation) show 4914/5354 and 4931/6456. If the paper's peak-memory number or the report's memory table comes from these fields, it is the gate's cap, not the method. eval_seg's RunRecord 'memory' peaks are inflated the same way.
findings.evidence: Code: gpu_reserve.py:31 `block = torch.empty(mib * 2 ** 20, dtype=torch.uint8, device=device)`. It runs before load_gaussians (run_mapping.py:142-143). There is no reset_peak_memory_stats before line 232 `peak_extract = torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated()...`. Cap arithmetic is confirmed by the OOM messages: cap 6000 -> '5.69 GiB allowed' (6000/16303*15.46), cap 3500 -> '3.32 GiB allowed'. Val logs: map_office_0.log `'peak_alloc_extract_mib': 4914.41..., 'peak_reserved_mib': 5354.0`. No GPU run with the reservation exists yet: stage_val.log shows the cc65f08 restart was still queued when it was stopped at 21:53.
findings.fix: At the end of apply(), after `del block`, call `torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats(device)`. Also save the reservation size in the timing dict, and mark peak_reserved_mib as not meaningful when a reservation is held. For the paper's timing run, use UAGS_GPU_RESERVE=0 on an idle GPU.

findings.title: Timing fields cannot fill the paper's run-time breakdown and overstate our per-keyframe cost
findings.problem: The paper promises four numbers: total ms, LSeg extraction ms, render+backward ms, and statistics/change test/re-admission ms. The code gives three. (a) update_view is timed as one block, so no field splits render+backward from the statistics. (b) ms_per_keyframe_field includes the view-hook baselines: with --baselines, NormLift/averaging and view count run inside update_view (vmf_field.py:323,352). (c) Since 5b21781, ms_per_keyframe_extract times extract_tokens plus the device-to-host copy. The host-to-device copy, upsample, normalisation and PCA projection (line 261), the rasterizer setup (262-264) and gaussian_depths are timed nowhere. So extract + update is not the total per keyframe. (d) The means include the first-call warm-up. usplat.runlog.Timer drops warm-up calls; this code does not.
findings.failure_scenario: If the paragraph is filled from the Tab I map logs, 'render and backward' and 'total' include the three baselines' hook work, and the total leaves out the upsample/PCA/raster setup. The paper would then state per-part times that were never measured.
findings.evidence: Smoke log (3 keyframes): ms_per_keyframe_field 123.96, versus 29.82 at 179 keyframes (map_office_0.log). So the first call costs ~3*124-2*30 = ~312 ms and adds ~1.6 ms (~5%) to the 179-frame mean. The office_0 fields: update 40.3, field 29.8, extract 65.9 ms. No timers exist inside vmf_field/bki_accumulate (grep of time/Timer/perf_counter found none). The old code (60d7796:219-223) timed extractor + upsample + PCA as 'extract'; the new comment says 'extractor (tokens) only'.
findings.fix: For the timing run: map one validation scene without --baselines (or time the hooks separately). Add synchronised timers inside update_view around the render+backward (bki accumulate) and around the statistics/change test. Time upsample+PCA+H2D and the rasterizer setup, and report their sum as the total. Drop the first keyframe (or use runlog.Timer with warm-up). Use UAGS_GPU_RESERVE=0 and fix the raw leak first.

findings.title: Mapping uses 176-180 keyframes, not the 180 frames the paper states
findings.where: scripts/run_mapping.py:183-200 (select, kf_trans 0.05 m AND kf_rot 5 deg); papers/main.tex:593, 616-617, 693, 768-775
findings.problem: select() drops a frame whose pose is within 5 cm and 5 deg of the last kept frame. The paper says each method maps on every 5th frame of Sequence_1 (180 frames), and the views figure uses 'M of the 180 mapping frames' with M=180. The 3D-GS map is also fit on 157 of the 180 frames (every 8th is held out for PSNR), while the paper says it is fit on the mapping frames.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader who reproduces Table I with all 180 frames gets slightly different fields. In the views figure, 'M=180' is really 176-180, and M=90 is 89 for room_1. All rows share the same frames, so the comparison stays fair.
findings.evidence: float32 count with the code's own _pose_gap (scratchpad/kf_select.py and an inline run): office_0 179, room_2 179, room_0 179, room_1 178, office_1 176, office_2 178, office_3 179, office_4 180. Views budgets: room_1 {10:10, 30:30, 90:89, 180:178}. The val logs agree: 'keyframes used 179' in both map logs. Map meta: holdout_every 8.
findings.fix: Change the text, for example: '180 frames; a frame within 5 cm and 5 deg of the previous kept one is skipped, which leaves 176-180', and say that the 3D-GS map holds out every 8th frame. Do not change the code: the val fields are already built this way.

findings.title: A failed reservation crashes a job that would otherwise fit
findings.problem: The reservation (cap-512 = 8227 MiB for a 9000 cap) is much larger than the job's real peak (4.8-5.7 GiB, ~2-3 GiB after the raw fix). torch.empty is not guarded. The gate checks free memory a few seconds before python reaches apply(). If another process takes memory in that window, the job dies at start with an OOM, even though its real need would still fit.
findings.failure_scenario: Here is one way it happens. The gate sees 11 GB free and starts the job. USGLoc's batch driver (bash batch_12s.sh, wait_gpu 7000/10000, 30 s poll) is not a python process, so the gate cannot see it. It launches train_locfeat during the ~5 s torch import. Free memory drops to ~7 GB, torch.empty(8227 MiB) raises, and replica_tab1.sh exits 1. No test number is produced, so it only costs a restart.
findings.evidence: gpu_reserve.py:31 has no try/except. gpu_gate.sh:35 only matches `pgrep -x python3|python`. The live USGLoc parent chain is: `bash .../batch_12s.sh cwd=/home/thanhnc/gauss_ws/src/usgloc` -> python3 run_7scenes.py.
findings.fix: Wrap the allocation in try/except torch.OutOfMemoryError. Retry with half the size, or return 0 with a warning. The per-process cap still applies either way.

findings.title: The 'never beside USGLoc' policy lives only in the launch environment; gate comments are stale
findings.problem: The README and stage_val.log say the val restart ran 'never beside a USGLoc job'. But the gate's default extra is 0, and its header still says parallel runs are allowed. replica_tab1.sh does not set the variable, and the value used is not recorded anywhere. Line 14 still says run_mapping applies the fraction with set_per_process_memory_fraction; it now goes through gpu_reserve. The cap is need/nvidia-smi-total times the torch total, so it is 0.971 x need (9000 -> 8739 MiB).
findings.failure_scenario: If STAGE=test is launched without the env var, the gate may start beside a running USGLoc python job, as the 15:18 and 20:16 eval OOMs did. Test numbers stay deterministic, but the run can crash, and the test map logs' ms/keyframe are taken on a shared GPU.
findings.evidence: gpu_gate.sh:21 `usgloc_extra=${UAGS_GPU_USGLOC_EXTRA_MIB:-0}`. stage_val.log: 'restart 2026-09-29 20:18:31 at cc65f08 (poll 5 s, never beside a USGLoc job, memory reserved at start)'. The OOM texts: 6000 -> '5.69 GiB allowed'.
findings.fix: Set UAGS_GPU_USGLOC_EXTRA_MIB (e.g. 100000) inside replica_tab1.sh/replica_views.sh/replica_tab3.sh, or change the gate default. Record the launch env in the report. Update the comments at lines 8-14.

checked_ok: Old (60d7796) vs new (HEAD) run_gsplat were run on the CPU with a fake extractor and a mock rasterizer on real Replica poses (scratchpad/equiv_mapping.py). The saved checkpoints are identical tensor by tensor (field state incl. None entries, PCA basis, baselines state, CSS ids and text path, config apart from --out). Cases: office_0 all 179 keyframes at downscale 8; room_2 with --max-keyframes 40 + --update-data Sequence_2 + --query (the change threshold 0.0155 is the same in both); office_1 at downscale 2 with the PCA randperm subsampling path. Output: 'DIFFS: none' in all three.

Keyframe set and order: select() is the same loop as the old run_sequence (evenly spaced subset, finite pose, near-duplicate test against the last kept frame; 'last' resets per sequence). The update sequence is selected without max_keyframes, as before.

PCA and centre: both versions fit on ds[0..19] (not keyframe-filtered), before any other RNG use. The CUDA randperm order is the same in both (fixed default seed, no RNG between). The centre comes from the same subsample.
Feature z per frame: LSeg extract_tokens returns fp32 contiguous (60,80,512). The .cpu() then .to(device) round trip is exact. upsample, normalise and project run as before.
`del clip` frees LSeg: get_extractor has no global cache, DenseCLIP holds no registry, and the closure cells are cleared (Python 3.12).

Val fields (made at 5b21781) and test fields (HEAD) use the same mapping code. git diff 5b21781..HEAD in usplat/ and scripts/ touches only run_mapping.py (reservation) and gpu_reserve.py on the mapping path. The working tree is clean.

fit_gs.py flags in replica_tab1.sh match the office_0 and room_2 map meta: dataset replica_semnerf, stride 5, iters 30000, max_gaussians 1e6, max_res 640, seed 0, holdout_every 8. The code_sha256 of gs_fit.py, datasets.py and fit_gs.py in both maps equals the current files. The only differing arg is log_every (1000 vs 500), which only logs.

gpu_reserve mechanics: the cap is set before any allocation. One large-pool block of cap-512 MiB is cached, and later >1 MiB allocations are split from it (default max_split_size). Small-pool segments use the 512 MiB margin. No torch.cuda.empty_cache in scripts/ or usplat/. The effective cap matches the OOM messages (5.69 / 3.32 GiB allowed).

gpu_gate.sh: the flock lock is taken non-blocking; free memory is re-checked under the lock; the child's exit code is returned and the lock released; a failed nvidia-smi read counts as 0 (wait); the poll interval is configurable. The USGLoc cwd detection finds the live job (pid 3725593 python3, cwd /home/thanhnc/gauss_ws/src/usgloc).

The per-keyframe timers wrap synchronize() on both sides, so the GPU work of the timed calls is charged correctly. peak_alloc_mib after the reset at line 282 is the mapping-phase peak and is not affected by the reservation.
The CPU-held tokens (179 x 9.4 MiB = ~1.7 GiB) fit in RAM (22 GiB available). No stale test maps or fields exist in uags_maps / uags_fields that the pipeline would silently reuse.
CPU tests: tests/test_state.py, test_pipeline_dryrun.py, test_feature_pca.py and test_baselines.py give 20 passed. `run_mapping.py --backend mock` runs to 'done.'
